data.name: Events.NoteOn.Description
data.value: Fires when a key is pressed in Control mode on a keyboard. Only subscribed keys are handled; every other key, and everything in Play mode, passes through.

data.name: Events.NoteOff.Description
data.value: Fires when a key is released on a keyboard. A release always goes where its press went.

data.name: Events.ControlChange.Description
data.value: Fires when a controller (knob, fader, pedal, CC) changes on a keyboard. Only the latest value is delivered.

data.name: Events.Device.Description
data.value: The keyboard to listen to. Leave empty for every keyboard registered.

data.name: Events.Note.Description
data.value: The key that triggers this event. Middle C is C4 (60).

data.name: Events.Controller.Description
data.value: The CC number (0-127), e.g. 64 for the sustain pedal.

data.name: Actions.SetMode.Description
data.value: Switches the router to Play or Control mode. In Play everything goes to the your app; in Control subscribed actions are executed.

data.name: Actions.SetMode.Target.Description
data.value: The mode to switch to, or Toggle to flip between Play and Control.

data.name: Actions.Routing.Description
data.value: Turns the router on or off. Off releases the keyboards so other apps can open them directly.

data.name: Actions.Routing.Switch.Description
data.value: Toggle, or always switch on or off.

data.name: ConfigFlow.StepDescriptionWindows
data.value: Select the keyboards to route and the loopback port (loopMIDI, or a Windows MIDI Services loopback). In the target app, disable the hardware keyboard and enable loopback port instead.

data.name: ConfigFlow.StepDescriptionMac
data.value: Select the keyboards to route. The router creates a virtual port. In the target app, disable hardware keyboard and enable the router's virtual port.

data.name: ConfigFlow.InputDevices.Description
data.value: MIDI inputs for the router. Inputs that are not selected are never opened.

data.name: ConfigFlow.OutputDevice.DescriptionWindows
data.value: Windows cannot create a virtual port for the router: create one with loopMIDI or the Windows MIDI Services settings and select it here.

data.name: ConfigFlow.OutputDevice.DescriptionMac
data.value: The router's own virtual port is recommended.

data.name: ConfigFlow.OutputDevice.Virtual
data.value: Virtual port created by MIDI Router

data.name: ConfigFlow.VirtualPortName.Description
data.value: The name the target app shows for the plugin.

data.name: ConfigFlow.StartMode.Description
data.value: The mode the router is in when Macro Deck starts.

data.name: ConfigFlow.ModeSound.Description
data.value: Beeps once for Play and twice for Control

data.name: ConfigFlow.Shortcuts.StepDescription
data.value: In Play mode - no action executed; in Control mode subscribed keys will run their actions. Here you can dedicate the key or CC for switching between modes.

data.name: ConfigFlow.Shortcuts.NoteDescription
data.value: Pick a key you don't need for playing, e.g. the lowest A0 (21) or highest C8 (108).

data.name: ConfigFlow.Shortcuts.ControllerDescription
data.value: 64 sustain, 66 sostenuto, 67 soft pedal. Counts as pressed from value 64.

data.name: ConfigFlow.Shortcuts.Listening
data.value: Listening: press the key or CC button on {device} you want as the shortcut. Click ✕ to stop.

data.name: ConfigFlow.Shortcuts.ActionHold
data.value: Control while held, back to Play on release

data.name: Issues.NotConfigured.Description
data.value: The router passes nothing through until you select at least one keyboard in its settings.

data.name: Issues.OutputNotConfigured.Description
data.value: Select the loopback port for the target app.

data.name: Issues.VirtualOutputUnsupported.Description
data.value: This system cannot create a virtual MIDI port. Create a loopback port (loopMIDI or Windows MIDI Services) and select it as the output.

data.name: Issues.OutputMissing.Description
data.value: Start the loopback app (e.g. loopMIDI) or recreate the port. The router reconnects by itself.

data.name: Issues.OutputFailed.Title
data.value: Output port '{port}' could not be opened

data.name: Issues.InputMissing.Description
data.value: The router opens it as soon as it is plugged in or wakes up.

data.name: Issues.InputBusy.Description
data.value: Another app holds the keyboard. Disable it in that app (for Dorico: Preferences > Play > MIDI Input Devices); the router retries by itself.

data.name: Issues.InputIsRouterOutput.Description
data.value: Reading the router's output back would create a feedback loop, so this input is ignored. Remove it from the keyboards.
